sections.name: File setup, ChartFilters, DemoBenchmarkData, FACETS
sections.title: Shared setup and category list
sections.what: Brings in shared types and helpers, re-exports the coverage helper, and defines the filter and data shapes. It also lists the five filter categories: industry, technology, company, country, and status.
sections.why: Names the filter options in one place.
sections.watch_out: The list is typed for four project fields. A new category needs a matching project field, or it will always show nothing.

sections.name: facetValues
sections.title: Values a project has for a category
sections.what: For company, returns every company name the project lists. For other categories, returns the single stored value unless it is blank or marked Not available.
sections.why: A project can belong to several companies, but other categories have one value per project.
sections.watch_out: Only the exact text Not available is ignored. Other placeholder words would be treated as real values.

sections.name: filterCohort
sections.title: Keeping projects that match the filters
sections.what: Keeps only projects that match every active filter. A filter with no chosen values does not restrict anything. It can also skip one named category, which lets that category's own options be counted.
sections.why: Skipping one category lets each option show how many results it would lead to.
sections.watch_out: An empty list of chosen values is treated as no filter, not as no matches.

sections.name: chartProjects
sections.title: Choosing which projects get plotted
sections.what: In the delivery view, keeps projects that have both a cost deviation and a schedule overrun figure. In other views, keeps projects with capital cost and capacity, then drops any that lack a usable bubble size.
sections.why: Only projects with real numbers on both axes can be drawn without misleading readers.
sections.watch_out: The two views use different rules, so the same project can appear in one chart and not the other.

sections.name: facetCounts
sections.title: Counting options in each category
sections.what: For each option of a category, counts how many projects would plot if that option were applied together with the other active filters. The results are sorted by count, then by name.
sections.why: Shows the user how many results each choice leads to before they pick it.
sections.watch_out: Counts use the plotting rules, so they can be lower than the number of matching projects.

sections.name: recommendSize
sections.title: Recommending a bubble size
sections.what: The portfolio view always uses equal dots. For other views it sizes dots by capacity if at most one fifth of plotted projects lack it, then by budget under the same rule, and otherwise uses equal dots. It returns a plain reason with each choice.
sections.why: Avoids sizing dots by a value that is missing for many projects.
sections.watch_out: The one fifth threshold is fixed in this code. Changing it changes the sizing of every chart.

sections.name: cohortInsights
sections.title: Plain-English insight lines
sections.what: Builds the summary lines for each view. The delivery view gets medians and a count of projects over both baselines. Other views get median capacity and budget, the highest budget project, and a caution that the chart measures scale rather than performance. An empty cut gets a note that missing values are not estimated.
sections.why: The text is written for readers who are not analysts, with the caveats built in.
sections.watch_out: The sentences assume the plotting rules guarantee values exist. Changing those rules without updating these lines can cause a crash.

summary: Filters projects by chosen categories and works out the chart points, option counts, bubble size choice, and plain-English insight lines for the scan charts.
purpose: Drives the chart filters in the Reality Scan: which projects are shown, how many projects each filter option leads to, and what to say about the result.
why: Likely reason: counts and insights should only use projects with comparable values. The messages in the code say that missing values are never estimated or set to zero.
how: Keeps the projects that match every active filter. For each option of a category, it counts how many projects would still plot if that option were applied alongside the other filters. For the delivery view it uses cost and schedule figures; for the other views it uses capital cost and capacity. It picks a bubble size rule based on how many plotted projects have usable values, and it builds insight sentences with coverage, medians, and the highest budget.
inputs: The list of projects, the current filter selections (a category name mapped to chosen values), a view name, and the category to count.
outputs: Filtered projects, the plotted projects, counts for each option, a bubble size recommendation with its reason, and a list of insight sentences.
risks: Medians are descriptive, not proof of cause. Several insight lines use non-empty assertions that assume values exist after the earlier plotting rules. If those rules change, the code could fail at run time.
debug: If a chart is empty, check the plotting rules in chartProjects for that view. If option counts look wrong, check facetValues and filterCohort. If insight text is wrong, check the median helper and the unit shown.
